note: Both sets are accurate on the claims they share (torque saturation 47,402.91 N•m, 15,000 N•m/s rate limit, rated generator speed 1173.7 rpm, high drivetrain damping, no torsional-vibration control loop). Set A additionally captures the key controller architecture facts: gain-scheduled PI control on speed error in Region 3, and the conditional that torque is computed as in Region 3 whenever the previous blade-pitch command is 1º or greater. Set B instead adds two correct but less central modeling details (single-DOF = shaft angular rotation, control goal = regulate generator speed) and omits the conditional logic and PI control method. No claim in either set is wrong, so A wins on coverage of important facts.
remarks: Both sets miss the stated trade-off of the conditional logic (improved output power quality at the expense of short-term generator/gearbox overloading) and the 10%-above-rated basis of the 47,402.91 N•m saturation, though the saturation quote itself conveys the 10% figure.
